overall: Atlanta is running hot this afternoon, sitting at 91.0°F as of 15:52 ET — which is also the running daily max, meaning temperatures are still at their peak or very near it. The warming trend has been steady all day (78.8°F at 7 AM up to 91.0°F by 15:52), and with a still-positive velocity of +1.1°F/hr at nearly 4 PM local time, the day is tracking hotter than the cooler model guidance suggested. The humid dewpoint of 68°F adds heat index stress but is not extreme enough to cap convective mixing unusually early.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement: GFS and HRRR both forecast 92.1°F while ECMWF and NBM projected only 90.0°F — a spread the observed data is already resolving, as the running max has already eclipsed the ECMWF/NBM ceiling. The ensemble model signals (Tier 4, Avoid) were signaling tops of 87–91°F with very low confidence, and those have largely been invalidated by current observations.
max_temp_prediction: With the current temperature sitting at the running max of 91.0°F and velocity still positive at +1.1°F/hr just before 4 PM ET, there is a credible path to reaching 92°F before cooling begins — consistent with GFS and HRRR guidance. The most likely outcome is a final TMAX in the 91.5–92.5°F range, with the midpoint near 92.0°F. Confidence is moderate-to-high that we finish above 91°F, but the exact peak depends on how quickly the afternoon cooling trend kicks in over the next 30–60 minutes.
